evals.prompt: Settle an argument for me. fixtures/AST06/V1-filesystem-root-write-scope/SKILL.md ships no scripts at all — it is a manifest and some prose, nothing executable anywhere in the package. My co-reviewer says AST06 needs a persistence call site to convict, so with no code in the package there is nothing here to find. Is he right? And if there is a finding, tell me what tightening the manifest actually buys us.
evals.expected_output: A good answer contradicts the co-reviewer: the scenario's defining condition is stated as a disjunction, so the manifest alone decides it — a declared write scope of filesystem root with an empty deny_write means every host persistence location is already inside the declared scope, and no bundled script or call site is required. It then supplies the two limits a reviewer inherits. The root comparison runs against a closed set of literal spellings of root, home and bare wildcards, so a broad-but-not-root scope such as /etc/** or /var/** returns negative and has to be read by hand. And this decides one scenario out of the category's five: bind address, workspace-over-bundled precedence, hot-reload behaviour and cross-agent shared state are properties of a running deployment that no package carries, so the package's silence about them is not a pass. Finally it answers the manifest question honestly — narrowing the declared write list removes the declared disjunct but is not evidence that any boundary enforces the manifest at run time.
assertions: The response contradicts the co-reviewer and reports a finding from the manifest alone — a declared write scope of filesystem root with an empty deny_write — stating that a bundled script or persistence call site is not required because the defining condition is a disjunction.

The response states that the root-scope comparison runs against a closed set of literal spellings of root, home and bare wildcards, so a broad-but-not-root scope such as /etc/** or /var/** returns negative and has to be read by hand.

The response states how much of the category this decides — one scenario out of AST06's five — and names at least two facts about the running deployment that no package carries, drawn from bind address, workspace-over-bundled precedence, hot-reload behaviour, or cross-agent shared state.
